title: Baron’s fiducia of pardon-to-be-obtained more probable — Wittich denies certainty as essential
source_text: CX. Sed probabilior est sententia Roberti Baronii, qui docet actum fidei salvificae, qui est causa instrumentalis justificationis, esse fiduciam veniae impetrandae. Quod tamen negant alii, si per fiduciam intelligatur certa ex fide persuasio. Negant enim certam persuasionem de remissione peccatorum, vel in praeterito, vel in futuro, esse actum essentialem fidei justificantis; ut videre est apud Wittichium in locis citatis: Quanvis non negant inter actus ad justificationem hominis requisitos, locum habere spem veniae impetrandae, seu fiduciam illam, quae dicitur in Scholis fiducia spei.
pass_a_gloss: But more probable is the opinion of Robert Baron, who teaches that the act of saving faith which is the instrumental cause of justification is trust of obtaining pardon. Which others nevertheless deny, if by trust is understood a certain persuasion from faith. For they deny that a certain persuasion of the remission of sins, whether in the past or in the future, is an essential act of justifying faith; as may be seen in Wittich in the places cited: although they do not deny that among the acts required for a person’s justification there is room for hope of obtaining pardon, or that trust which in the Schools is called trust of hope.
pass_b_english: More probable: Robert Baron — the instrumental justifying act is fiducia of pardon to be obtained.
Others deny this if “fiducia” means certain faith-persuasion of remission (past or future) as essential; so Wittich.
They still allow, among required acts, hope of obtaining pardon — Scholastic fiducia spei.

choices.english: more probable is Robert Baron’s opinion
choices.why: Le Blanc ranks Baron above present-remission fiducia.
